package_info.why_malicious: The attack leverages a timing side-channel in the npm registry API to reveal the existence of private package names, enabling attackers to create malicious clones or typosquatted packages for supply chain attacks.

execution_context.file_location: N/A (external API request to npm registry)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends repeated GET requests to the npm registry for specific package names, measures the response time for 404 errors, and infers whether a private package exists based on timing differences.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it systematically probes the registry for package existence using timing as a side-channel, which is not a standard or legitimate use of the API.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would be to check for public package existence or download packages, not to infer private package names via timing analysis.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use might include checking for public package availability before publishing, but not for private package enumeration.
key_indicators: Automated, repeated GET requests for package names
Measurement and analysis of HTTP response times for 404 errors
Focus on organization-scoped or likely-private package names

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends repeated GET requests to the npm registry for candidate package names, measuring response times for 404 errors.
attack_chain.leads_to: Identification of private package names used by the target organization.

attack_chain.action: Attacker registers a public package with the same or similar name as the discovered private package (typosquatting or direct impersonation).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious package is available publicly under a name trusted by the target organization.

attack_chain.action: Target organization or its developers accidentally install the malicious clone, leading to potential supply chain compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in the target environment.

behavioral_signatures: Automated enumeration of package names via npm registry API
Analysis of HTTP response times for 404 errors
Burst or pattern of requests targeting organization-scoped package names
file_indicators: N/A (attack is external and does not leave file artifacts on the target system)
network_indicators: High-frequency GET requests to https://registry.npmjs.org/ for non-existent or private package names
Patterns of requests targeting @organization/* package namespaces
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for automated or high-frequency GET requests to the npm registry for package names, especially those matching internal or organization-scoped patterns. Look for clients measuring response times and correlating them with package existence. Alert on attempts to register public packages with names similar to known private packages.
